design.label: lenient alias match (committed)
design.label_2: strict exact match, recomputed from the frozen eval set

what_these_are: Exact functions of each measured certificate's counts, and exact counts of disagreement between two matching rules. The strict rule is not a better labeller; counting its disagreements as lenient errors bounds one identified ambiguity of the labelling rule, not its label error.

sensitivity.meaning: The confidence at which this certificate's budget still clears if that many labels are wrong in the named direction. It is not a probability that the detector is within budget.
sensitivity.direction: Two label errors flatter the bound: a flagged item labelled positive that is really clean (one more false positive and one more negative), and an unflagged item labelled negative that is really positive (one fewer negative). The other two -- a flagged negative that is really positive, an unflagged positive that is really clean -- make the bound conservative and are never used to tighten it. Errors of both kinds together cost more than either ladder shows alone.

kappa.estimator: Cohen's kappa, percentile bootstrap over pairs

disputes.worst_case_meaning: Every disagreement among the pairs counted against the primary label: a worst case over the pairs, not a bound on the truth.

whole_file.joint_level: each bound holds at 1 - alpha; both hold together at >= 0.9000, by the union bound
whole_file.estimator: exact hypergeometric upper bounds over the flagged positives and over the unflagged negatives, each from its double-labelled items
whole_file.assumes: the double-labelled items in each pool are a simple random sample of that pool; Warrant cannot see how they were chosen
whole_file.confidence_meaning: The certificate's confidence if the disputes are at those bounds and every one is a primary error. A sensitivity evaluated at upper confidence bounds: not a joint confidence, and not to be combined with the bounds' level into one figure.

second_review.cannot_check: A disagreement is not an error, and an agreement is not a correct label: two reviewers who were both wrong, or who both saw the score, agree and are counted clean. Warrant cannot see whether reviewers were blind to the score or how the double-labelled items were chosen.

sensitivity.meaning: The confidence at which this certificate's budget still clears if that many labels are wrong in the named direction. It is not a probability that the detector is within budget.
sensitivity.direction: Two label errors flatter the bound: a flagged item labelled positive that is really clean (one more false positive and one more negative), and an unflagged item labelled negative that is really positive (one fewer negative). Errors of both kinds together cost more than either ladder shows alone.
